newsitem.title: JAPAN: NCB says capital ratio at 8.7-8.9 pct at end-March.
newsitem.headline: NCB says capital ratio at 8.7-8.9 pct at end-March.

text.p: Japan's Nippon Credit Bank Ltd said on Monday that its preliminary international capital adequacy ratio stood at between 8.7 percent and 8.9 percent at the end of the fiscal year on March 31.
A NCB official disclosed the data, without giving any further details. The ratio stood at 8.38 percent a year ago.
Under the rules of the Bank for International Settlements (BIS), Japanese banks operating internationally need to have capital equivalent to eight percent of risk-weighted assets.
Unlike many countries, Japanese authorities allow banks to include unrealised profits on securities holdings as part of capital.

The Japanese financial daily Nihon Keizai Shimbun reported last week that an expected net loss for the second consecutive year and liquidation of its bad loans will make it almost impossible for the ailing NCB to meet capital adequacy requirements of globally operating banks.
The paper said NCB may withdraw from its overseas operations under a restructuring plan now being worked out.
The bank quickly denied the report on Thursday, saying that it plans to unveil its restructuring plan in early April, but that nothing had been decided.
